garageRules.rule: Ley de Establecimientos Mercantiles, Art. 50 (2023 reform): regulated tariffs for estacionamientos públicos
garageRules.detail: Garages must charge in 15-minute fractions from the first hour, at the same price for each fraction (previously the full first hour was charged). Each of the 16 alcaldías authorizes tariffs by zone, road type and traffic flow; tariffs are verified annually and published in the Gaceta Oficial. Differentiated rates by vehicle size are no longer allowed. The 2023 reform also made garages liable for damage or theft.

reservations.policy: Restaurants may ask for a credit card to secure a reservation; if it is changed or missed outside the restaurant's cancellation window, the restaurant (not OpenTable) decides whether and how much to charge, and only the restaurant can refund. The policy is shown at booking and in the confirmation email. The restaurant sees only the card's last four digits and type.
reservations.bookingHorizon: Restaurants set how far ahead guests can book, reportedly from 1 to 365 days; most release 14-30 days ahead.
reservations.note: Help page is client-rendered and returned no text to the fetch tool; this is a search summary.

reservations.policy: From late 2025 (remaining restaurants early 2026) OpenTable adds a 2% service fee to online payments including no-show fees, deposits and prepaid experiences; restaurants may absorb it or pass it to the diner. Example: Pizzata Pizzeria & Birreria (Philadelphia) charges a $15 per-person no-show fee with a 20-minute grace period.
reservations.note: Philadelphia Inquirer report of 2026-01-14 quoting an OpenTable spokesperson; read directly, but it is a news report, not OpenTable's own page.

reservations.policy: Restaurants that charge a cancellation fee, require a card on file, or take prepayment make Resy ask for a card at booking. Cancellation timing and fee are shown before booking and in the confirmation. Fees are not charged automatically: the restaurant charges them manually in Resy OS. A no-show can mean a fee or forfeiting a prepayment.
reservations.bookingHorizon: Restaurant-set rolling window; commonly 14-30 days, some 60-90. One count of 50 confirmed Resy rooms: 12 open 30 days ahead, 8 at 14, 7 at 21, 6 at 28; range 6-60 days.
reservations.note: Resy help pages are client-rendered; search summary. Booking-window counts come from reservationfinder.io, a third party.

reservationRules.jurisdiction: Quebec (not one of the eight towns; the nearest Canadian rule and a model for the others)
reservationRules.rule: Maximum no-show fee $10 per person, for reservations of 2 or more. No fee if cancelled at least 3 hours before, if at least one member of the party shows up, or if the merchant failed its obligations. The fee must be disclosed before booking, cancellation must be easy, a reminder with a cancellation link must be sent 6-48 hours before, and no-show fees may not be charged in advance.

reservationRules.jurisdiction: New York, Los Angeles, New Haven, Toronto, Vancouver, London, Dublin, Mexico City
reservationRules.note: No town- or state/province-level rule capping or regulating restaurant no-show fees was found for any of the eight towns.

values.statement: Trade-in Value is KBB's estimate of what a consumer can expect to receive from a dealer for a trade-in vehicle, assuming an accurate appraisal of condition. 'This value will likely be less than the Kelley Blue Book Private Party Value because the reselling dealer incurs the cost of safety inspections, reconditioning and other costs of doing business.' Private Party Value is 'the starting point for negotiation of a used-car sale between a private buyer and seller', an 'as is' value without warranties.
values.gapNote: KBB's definitions page gives no fixed percentage; the gap is per vehicle.

values.statement: Search summaries report trade-in values averaging 10-20% below private party (attributed to KBB), private sales yielding 15-25% more, and a Carvana-attributed study showing private-party values 46% above dealer offers on average (75% under $20,000; 43% over $20,000).
values.note: Secondary blogs, not KBB, Edmunds or Carvana pages; treat as unverified ranges.

values.statement: Average trade-in equity reached a record $13,330 in Q2 2026. Average transaction price of 3-year-old used vehicles $32,461 in Q2 2026 (up 4% year over year); $31,216 in Q2 2025.

transfer.statement: Vehicle permit (all vehicles) $32; licence plate with permit $59 if new plates are needed. The seller is legally required to give the buyer a $20 Used Vehicle Information Package. Requires ID, CDMX proof of address, proof of ownership, current tarjeta de circulación, payment, and no tenencia debts.
